module_title: Basics of the Plant Kingdom and Vascular Tissues
introduction: The Plant Kingdom consists of multicellular, eukaryotic, and autotrophic organisms. At this level, we divide the plant kingdom into basic functional categories and understand the 'plumbing system' that keeps them alive.

core_concepts.title: Broad Classification of Plants
core_concepts.description:
1. Cryptogams (Seedless Plants): Lower plants that do not produce flowers or seeds. They reproduce via 'spores'. (Examples: Algae, Mosses, Ferns). 
2. Phanerogams (Seed-Bearing Plants): Higher plants that produce seeds. (Examples: Pine trees, Mango trees, Rose bushes).

core_concepts.title: Vascular Tissues (The Plumbing System)
core_concepts.description:
Plants need a transport system to move water from the roots and food from the leaves. 
1. Xylem: Transports 'Water and Minerals' from the roots to the rest of the plant. 
2. Phloem: Transports 'Food' (prepared in the leaves by photosynthesis) to all other parts of the plant.

core_concepts.title: Photosynthesis (Basic)
core_concepts.description:
The process by which green plants make their own food using Sunlight, Carbon Dioxide ($CO_2$), and Water ($H_2O$) in the presence of Chlorophyll. 
Equation: $6CO_2 + 6H_2O \xrightarrow{\text{Sunlight/Chlorophyll}} C_6H_{12}O_6 \text{ (Glucose)} + 6O_2 \text{ (Oxygen)}$.

important_entities.name: Direction of Transport
important_entities.significance: Xylem transport is strictly 'Unidirectional' (it only moves UP from the roots to the leaves). Phloem transport is 'Bidirectional' (food moves both UP and DOWN depending on where the plant needs it).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Because fungi (like mushrooms) grow in the soil, students often assume they belong to the Plant Kingdom. They DO NOT. Fungi are heterotrophic (they lack chlorophyll and cannot make their own food) and belong to their own entirely separate kingdom.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the phonetic sounds: Xylem transports 'Jal' (Hindi for water). Phloem transports 'Phal' (Hindi for fruit/food).

exam_strategy_tips: A guaranteed question in SSC and Railway exams: 'Which complex tissue is responsible for the transport of food in plants?' Answer: Phloem.
